title: ASCOU — Racing-Inspired Apparel Design
summary: Two racing-inspired apparel graphic commissions developed through concept variations, brand integration, and client-led revisions.
facts: Two separate commissioned shirt designs: ASCO 101 and ASCOU Pit Stop
Multiple concept options and client-directed revisions
Final digital artwork delivered; physical shirt production not confirmed
mediaNote: Final digital designs: ASCO 101 (first) and ASCOU Pit Stop (second). Artwork is not a photograph of a manufactured shirt.
fullCaseHtml:
For ASCOU at Allison-Smith Company, I completed two racing-inspired T-shirt graphic commissions in summer 2026: an ASCO 101 design and an ASCOU Pit Stop design.

My contribution focused on graphic composition, adapting and manipulating existing visual assets, typography, layout, branding, and revisions. I did not hand-illustrate the cars, people, or other graphics from scratch. I developed alternative treatments, responded to client feedback, and prepared the selected digital artwork for delivery.

Commission 01: ASCO 101 Racing Graphic

The first brief called for a NASCAR-inspired front-and-back shirt graphic featuring “ASCO 101,” “Learn. Apply. Lead.,” a No. 43 race car, and ASCOU branding. I presented multiple treatments and mockups. After a client request to change the car style, I revised the composition around a red vintage-inspired car and provided additional variations. The client selected a preferred option, and I delivered the final transparent artwork in August 2026.

Commission 02: ASCOU Pit Stop

The second assignment allowed a more open-ended pit stop and racetrack direction. I presented three initial concepts for review. The client selected a direction and requested revisions to figures, racing details, lettering, and a separate “ASCOU PIT STOP” back-of-shirt graphic. I refined the No. 43 car and other details in subsequent revisions and delivered the final artwork on September 2, 2026.

Design Approach and Delivery

Both commissions required translating visual references into branded compositions through asset selection, image manipulation, typography, layout, and client-directed revisions. The result was two client-approved digital design commissions with final artwork delivered. Physical shirt manufacturing has not been confirmed, so this page presents the digital designs rather than claiming a completed merchandise run.
